overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 15
overview.text: In this lesson, you will investigate compound sentences. A compound sentence joined by 'and' is true only when both constituent sentences are true (intersection), while a compound sentence joined by 'or' is true when at least one constituent sentence is true (union).
outcomes: Describe the solution set of two equations or inequalities joined by the connective 'and' as the intersection of their individual solution sets.
Describe the solution set of two equations or inequalities joined by the connective 'or' as the union of their individual solution sets.
Graph compound sentences on the real number line.
overview.teacherInsight: Connect 'and' to simultaneous conditions (both must hold) and 'or' to alternative choices (at least one must hold). In logic, mathematical 'or' is always inclusive unless stated otherwise.

content.html:
Compound Sentence Intersection & Union Visualizer

Toggle between AND (Intersection $\cap$) and OR (Union $\cup$) for the sentence: $x - 15 = 5$ [connective] $2x + 5 = 1$.

Sentence 1: $x - 15 = 5$ x = 20
Sentence 2: $2x + 5 = 1$ x = -2
Compound Solution Set:
{-2, 20}
Under OR: Any value that makes EITHER equation true is a solution.

vocabulary.definition: A compound sentence that is true only if both of its component statements are simultaneously true. Corresponding to set intersection (∩).
A compound sentence that is true if at least one of its component statements is true. Corresponding to set union (∪).
The set of elements belonging to both sets A and B (A ∩ B).
The set of elements belonging to set A, set B, or both (A ∪ B).

practiceQuestions.question: What is the solution set to the compound sentence: $x - 15 = 5$ or $2x + 5 = 1$?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Solving $x - 15 = 5 \implies x = 20$. Solving $2x + 5 = 1 \implies 2x = -4 \implies x = -2$. Joined by 'or', the solution set is the union: $\{-2, 20\}$.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the solution set to the compound sentence: $x > 5$ AND $x < 2$?
options: The empty set $\emptyset$ (no real number can be both greater than 5 and less than 2)
practiceQuestions.explanation: Joined by 'and', a value must satisfy both conditions simultaneously. Since no number is both $> 5$ and $< 2$, the intersection is empty ($\{ \}$ or $\emptyset$).
